introduction_markdown: General Certificate of Education (GCE) Board, Ordinary Level, June 2024. Additional Mathematics 2 (code 0575), Paper 2. Duration: two and a half hours. Answer ALL questions in SECTION A and ANY TWO questions from EITHER SECTION B or SECTION C. In Sections B and C, all questions carry equal marks. Candidates are expected to answer a combination of Section A and Section B OR Section A and Section C, but NOT a combination of all three. Section A: Pure Mathematics (compulsory, answer all questions, questions 1 to 8). Section B: Mechanics (answer any two questions, questions 9 to 11; if this section is chosen, Section C may not be chosen). Section C: Statistics and Probability (answer any two questions, questions 12 to 14; if this section is chosen, Section B may not be chosen). All necessary working must be shown. No marks will be awarded for answers without brief statements showing how the answers have been obtained. Electronic calculators and Formulae Booklets are allowed. Where necessary take g as 10 m s^-2.

questions.enonce_markdown:
8. (i)

![fig-1](gce-ol-additional-maths-2024-p2-officiel-cameroun_exercice_8_fig_1.png)

The diagram above shows a rectangular grazing area of a sheep bounded by an existing wall and barbwire on the sides labelled $x$ and $k$. Given that the grazing area is $162\,\text{m}^2$.

a) Show that the perimeter of grazing area, $P$, is given as $P=2x+\dfrac{162}{x}$. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The wall is one side of the rectangle, so barbwire is needed only on the two sides of length $x$ and the side of length $k$:

$$P=2x+k.$$

The area is $x\times k=162$, so $k=\dfrac{162}{x}$. Substitute:

$$P=2x+\frac{162}{x}.\qquad\text{(shown)}$$

questions.enonce_markdown: (i)(b) Find the minimum perimeter of the barbwire. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
$P=2x+162x^{-1}$, so

$$\frac{dP}{dx}=2-\frac{162}{x^2}.$$

At a stationary point $\dfrac{dP}{dx}=0$: $2=\dfrac{162}{x^2}$, so $x^2=81$ and $x=9$ (a length, so $x>0$).

Nature: $\dfrac{d^2P}{dx^2}=\dfrac{324}{x^3}$, which is $\dfrac{324}{729}>0$ at $x=9$, so this is a **minimum**.

Minimum value: $P=2(9)+\dfrac{162}{9}=18+18=36$.

(Here $k=162/9=18$ m.)

**Answer: the minimum length of barbwire is $36$ m.**

$$\int(3x-x^2)\,dx=\frac{3x^2}{2}-\frac{x^3}{3}+c.$$

**Answer: $\dfrac{3}{2}x^2-\dfrac13x^3+c$.**
